title: Tachometer: standardized token-velocity microbenchmark suite for core models
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build and stabilize a compact, reproducible microbenchmark harness ("tachometer") to measure tokens-per-second (TPS) and p95 latency across core model variants. The harness must support synthetic and replay workloads, KV-cache warmup modes, variable context lengths, and multi-concurrency sweeps. Goal is a lightweight, CI-run suite that produces deterministic fingerprints for regression detection and integrates with Grafana/alerting.
acceptance_criteria: Runnable command (CI job) that executes a canonical benchmark matrix (models, batch sizes, seq lengths, concurrency) and emits JSON results to S3/GCS
p95 and mean TPS reported per-model/per-run with stable fingerprinting hash that changes only on meaningful runtime or model changes
KV-warm and KV-cold modes available; warm mode should prepopulate KV cache using a documented warmup procedure
Regression detector job that compares current run to baseline and flags >5% TPS drop or >10% p95 increase, creating an alert ticket in Linear
Integrations: Grafana dashboard with historical series, Prometheus metrics exported by harness, and a Slack alert channel for failures/regressions
Documentation: runbook describing how to add new models, how to interpret fingerprints, and how to triage common noise sources (OOM, host variance)
implementation_notes: Harness implemented as a single Python CLI (bench_tacho) that drives the existing inference runtime through the public SDK and a low-level RPC path for high-fidelity timing
Workloads: 1) synthetic prompt generation (fixed seed, repeated), 2) replay of anonymized real traffic traces (sampled), 3) burst+steady multi-stage scenario for p95 amplification
Timing: measure end-to-end token emit time and internal kernel timing when supported; prefer server-side timestamps for consistency
Fingerprinting: canonicalize result buckets (per-token throughput, p95) and compute a SHA256 over normalized CSV; store artifact with run metadata
CI: nightly baseline run and PR gating cheap smoke runs (subset of the matrix) to detect regressions early
Noise mitigation: run each cell N times (N configurable, default 3), use median for TPS and 95th for p95; discard runs with >10% CPU/GPU utilization deviation compared to baseline host metrics
test_plan: Unit tests for harness parsing and result normalization
Integration test that runs a single-model, single-concurrency job in CI using a tiny test model (fast) to validate plumbing
E2E nightly job that runs full matrix and stores artifacts; verify Grafana ingestion and alert firing for injected regressions
Chaos test to simulate KV cache cold-start: clear caches between runs and verify warm/cold delta is measured
monitoring: Export Prometheus metrics: bench_run_duration_seconds, bench_tps, bench_p95_ms, bench_fingerprint_hash
Grafana dashboard panels: TPS time-series, p95 heatmap by model x seq_len, regression alert history
Alert rules: regression_detected -> create Linear ticket + post to #infra-bench-alerts on Slack
Store artifacts: per-run JSON, normalized CSV, and fingerprint hash in s3://redwood-bench-artifacts/tachometer/YYYYMMDD/
rollout_plan: Phase 1: land harness code and small-matrix CI smoke (P0 gating only) - responsible eng pair: Rafael + Anika
Phase 2: enable nightly full-matrix runs and Grafana dashboards; set soft alert threshold (warn at 3% TPS drop)
Phase 3: tighten detection threshold to production levels (5% TPS / 10% p95) and enable auto-ticketing
Phase 4: onboarding docs and internal demo; invite model owners to subscribe to alerts
